title: Filter stalled schemas in SQL before limiting candidates
answers: Why does a limited stalled-sync sweep miss stopped schemas?
Where should the latest-run filter be applied?
How should malformed or timezone-free run stamps be handled?
body:
Invariant: Compute and filter by the latest run stamp in SQL before applying the candidate limit; products/warehouse_sources/backend/stalled_schedules.py:stalled_schema_queryset annotates latest_run_at and uses it for stalled_after.
Ordering: products/warehouse_sources/backend/stalled_schedules.py:find_stalled_schemas orders by latest_run_at before slicing and calculates stalled_for from the same annotation.
Failure: Filtering quiet schemas in Python after LIMIT can let them consume every slot; filtering before LIMIT loads every quiet candidate on each sweep.
Cast guard: products/warehouse_sources/backend/stalled_schedules.py:_AWARE_ISO_TIMESTAMP gates the JSON timestamp cast to offset-bearing ISO strings; missing or nonmatching stamps become NULL, allowing PostgreSQL GREATEST to fall back to last_synced_at.
Python counterpart: products/warehouse_sources/backend/models/external_data_schema.py:ExternalDataSchema.last_full_run returns None for parsing failures or naive timestamps; products/warehouse_sources/backend/temporal/data_imports/workflow_activities/create_job_model.py:_fast_return_eligible uses that property.
Constraints: Preserve timezone rejection: an unguarded SQL cast can raise on an unparseable string, and PostgreSQL interprets a naive timestamp in the session timezone, inventing freshness.
applies: Stalled-schema sweep and repair candidate queries, and readers parsing the JSON last_full_run_at stamp.
